cards.text: By now Abraham is old and well along in years, and the LORD has blessed him in every way. So he calls in his chief servant, the man who manages everything he owns. I bet that servant walked in hoping for a raise.
Abraham tells him, "Place your hand under my thigh," and then has him swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth. Friend, when the boss opens with THAT, you are NOT getting a raise.

cards.question: Abraham has his chief servant swear an oath by the LORD. What is the oath about?

answers.text: Finding a wife for his son Isaac

cards.question: True or false: Abraham wants his servant to find Isaac a wife from the daughters of the Canaanites living around him.
Instead, Abraham sends the servant to his own country and his own ___ to find Isaac a wife.

cards.text: The servant has a question first: "What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?" Friend, this man READS the fine print, and I respect it.

cards.question: The servant asks if he should take Isaac back to Abraham's homeland if the woman won't come. What does Abraham say?

answers.text: Take Isaac back if you must

cards.text: Then Abraham reminds him who's really running this trip. The LORD brought Abraham from his father's house and his native land, and promised him on oath, "To your offspring I will give this land".

cards.question: Abraham is sure the LORD will help his servant find a wife for Isaac. What does he say the LORD will send ahead of the servant?
True or false: Abraham says that if the woman won't come, his servant is released from the oath.

cards.text: So the servant places his hand under Abraham's thigh and swears the oath. No pen, no paperwork, no sleeping on it. The man is IN.

The servant takes ten of his master's camels and all kinds of good things, and heads for the hometown of Nahor, Abraham's brother, in Aram-naharaim. TEN camels, friend, and I get nervous showing up with ONE cookie box.

cards.question: As evening comes, the servant makes his camels kneel down near the ___ outside the town.

cards.text: It's the time when the women come out to draw water. "O LORD, God of my master Abraham," the servant prays, "please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham."

cards.question: The servant asks the LORD for a sign. He'll ask a girl at the spring for a drink. What will the right girl do?

answers.text: Offer to water his camels too
Ask him to wait for her father
Ask him where his master lives

cards.text: Before the servant has even finished praying, out comes a young woman named Rebekah with her jar on her shoulder. Friend, the man didn't even get to amen, and I have waited LONGER for my oven to preheat.
Rebekah is very beautiful. She goes down to the spring, fills her jar and comes back up.

cards.question: True or false: When Rebekah comes back up from the spring, the servant waits for her to come over to him.

cards.text: He runs to her and asks for a little water, and she says, "Drink, my lord," and quickly gives him a drink from her jar. Half the sign, DONE.

cards.question: Half the sign is done. After the servant drinks, what does Rebekah tell him?

answers.text: She'll draw water for his camels too
He should rest before going on
Her father will water his camels

cards.text: She quickly empties her jar into the trough and runs back to the well to draw more, until she's watered every one of his camels. TEN camels, friend, and I get winded hopping my gold base across the bakery ONE time.

cards.question: While Rebekah waters the camels, the servant watches her silently. What is he waiting to see?

answers.text: If the LORD made his trip a success
If she will ask him to pay her
If her family will come out to him

cards.question: When the camels finish drinking, the servant takes out a gold ___ and two gold ___ for Rebekah.

cards.text: Then he asks her, "Whose daughter are you?" and whether there's room in her father's house for them to spend the night. Ten camels, a pile of gold and NO place to stay, friend.

cards.question: Rebekah says she's the daughter of Bethuel. Whose granddaughter is she?
Then Rebekah adds that her family has plenty of straw and ___, and a place for the servant to spend the night.

cards.text: Then the man bows down and worships the LORD. Prayer asked, prayer answered, and he does NOT skip the thank you.

cards.question: The servant blesses the LORD, the God of his master Abraham. What does he praise Him for?

answers.text: His kindness and faithfulness to Abraham
Sending rain for the thirsty camels

cards.text: Then he adds, "As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives." We'll leave it right there for now, friend, and trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The joke 'when the boss opens with THAT' turns the hand-under-the-thigh oath gesture into a workplace punchline. It invites an innuendo reading of the gesture.

rule.text: No cursing, crude humor, innuendo, or social or political commentary.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'So the servant places his hand… swears the oath.' 'No pen, no paperwork, no sleeping on it.' 'The man is IN.' Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choice cards can only be answered by luck or prior knowledge. Card 3 asks what the oath is about, but no earlier card mentions Isaac or a wife. Card 4 asks about the Canaanites, who haven't been mentioned. Card 7 asks Abraham's reply, card 9 asks what the LORD will send ahead, and card 10 is a true or false on the release from the oath. The story cards give no context to reason from. That is far more than a few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card calls Nahor 'Abraham's brother', but that fact comes from Genesis 24:15, not 24:10. The card cites only Genesis 24:10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Rebekah's first appearance calls her only 'a young woman named Rebekah'. Genesis 24:15 says right away who she is: the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor. Fixing this would give away card 14 (whose granddaughter she is), so card 14 must be reworked too.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of Rebekah's line ('plenty of straw and ___'). It doesn't test meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. 'feed' is animal fodder that pairs naturally with straw, while 'silver' is a precious metal. This makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The closing line 'We'll leave it right there for now, friend, and trust me, this story is NOT done.' nearly copies the doc's example line instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
